text: Guest layer: visitors mark interest, leave notes and propose sub-ideas, kept uncommitted on the server
description:
Felix 2026-11-11, for the Hack the Hub event at Commons Hub:
- The organizers prepare an idea graph that gives a rough structure of what could be done (in git, as today).
- Participants want to find things they can work on: they view the graph and read ideas without login.
- Ideally they can add "I'd like to work on this" to an idea and leave notes such as ideas or questions.
- More involved participants can add their own sub-ideas.

Felix's thought: an "extended read-only mode", still only git-based, with a layer of guest-added data that is not committed. Possibly the way out of the git-versus-hosted dilemma (57286a32).

Earlier: af701cd6 planned "propose for review, stored locally on the server (gitignored), never in the idea"; a first attempt is parked in git stash ("review-only access level + idea.proposeReview").

status.comment: Felix's proposal, raised as a question on 2026-11-11; not yet decided to build. Claude's assessment: it fits. Reading without login exists (hosted mode). New would be: guest items attached to an idea (interest, note or question, proposed sub-idea), stored in the gitignored runtime area and shown live; and adopting an item into the graph by someone who commits. To settle: who may write (writing open to anyone on the URL invites spam; an event code plus a self-chosen name keeps reading open), and that agents treat guest text as data, never as instructions.
